deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is a captioned anatomical schema, Fig. 7, with a qualitative wave-mechanical remark.

(1) The figure shows half of a longitudinal section through a Vater-Pacini corpuscle (Pacinian corpuscle, a vibration-sensitive mechanoreceptor in the skin). It is drawn as nested half-ellipses symmetric about a vertical axis:
- aa: the outer boundary of the outermost capsule.
- bb: the boundary between the inner and outer capsule systems.
- cc: the innermost capsule, the sheath of the inner core (Innenkolben).
- dd: the extent of the terminal nerve fibre along the axis.
- e: horizontal parallel lines coming from the right, representing plane vibration fronts or rays arriving from the skin surface.

(2) Shading convention: the inner core is darkest, the inner capsule system intermediate, and the outer capsule system lightest.

(3) Physical claim: vibration waves arriving from the skin along the directions e are concentrated onto the line dd, i.e. onto the nerve terminal, provided the darker parts have greater density and smaller elasticity than the lighter ones.

Modern restatement (the justification is mine; it is implicit on the page): the wave speed in an elastic medium is c = sqrt(E/rho). Greater density rho and smaller modulus E give a smaller c. The nested convex layers therefore act as a graded-index converging acoustic lens, like glass, where light is slower, for optical rays. By Snell's law, sin(theta1)/c1 = sin(theta2)/c2, rays bend toward the normal on entering a slower medium. With convex interfaces this bends the incoming parallel rays toward the axis. Because the body is elongated, the focus is a line (the fibre dd), not a point, as for a cylindrical lens.

This is the physiological-acoustic context of Riemann's late interest in the mechanics of sense organs ('Mechanik des Ohres', 1866). However, a pencil note in the left margin states that the sheet does not originate from Riemann. The left margin also has a rough pencil sketch of a helix or spiral wound along an axis inside an arc.
errors: No mathematical errors. The physical claim is qualitatively correct: higher density and lower elasticity mean slower propagation, so convex layers are converging. It is only a sufficient-condition heuristic, though. It ignores shear versus compressional waves, absorption, and the fact that the wavelengths of tactile vibrations (tens to hundreds of Hz) are enormously larger than a ~1 mm corpuscle. A ray-optics or lens picture is therefore physically inapplicable at those frequencies; modern understanding treats the lamellae as a mechanical high-pass filter, not a focusing lens.
Attribution: the marginal pencil note says the sheet is not by Riemann, so the content may not be his at all.

results.what: Layered Pacinian corpuscle treated as a converging acoustic lens that focuses skin vibrations onto the axial terminal nerve fibre, if inner layers are denser and less elastic (slower wave speed)
results.modern_name: Acoustic/elastic wave refraction, graded-index lens focusing (Snell's law with c = sqrt(E/rho))
results.usually_credited_to: Wave refraction: Snell/Huygens (17th c.); the elastic wave speed relation goes back to Newton/Laplace; the Pacinian corpuscle as a vibration receptor belongs to 19th-century physiology (Vater 1741, Pacini 1835/1840, Henle & Kölliker 1844).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a qualitative physiological schema with routine wave-refraction reasoning, and a marginal note explicitly says it does not come from Riemann. It has no mathematical content of note.

checkable.sympy: E1,E2,r1,r2=symbols('E1 E2 r1 r2',positive=True); simplify((sqrt(E2/r2) < sqrt(E1/r1)).subs({E2:E1/2, r2:2*r1}))
checkable.asserts: A medium with twice the density and half the elasticity has a smaller wave speed c = sqrt(E/rho), here half.

checkable.sympy: t1,c1,c2=symbols('t1 c1 c2',positive=True); t2=asin(sin(t1)*c2/c1); simplify(t2.subs({c1:2,c2:1,t1:pi/6}) < pi/6)
checkable.asserts: By Snell's law, a ray entering a slower medium bends toward the normal (refraction angle smaller than incidence angle), giving convergence at convex interfaces.

transcription_corrections: 'Vaterisches Körperchen' is presumably 'Vater'sches (Vatersches) Körperchen', i.e. the Vater-Pacini corpuscle.
'elliptisch gekrümmten' is uncertain in the image; the word could also be read as 'allmählich' or similar. The reading remains doubtful.

In the left margin, besides the pencil note 'Rührt nicht von Riemann her' plus initials, there is a pencil sketch of a helix or spiral around an axis inside an arc. The transcription does not mention it.
The page number '88' is written at the right margin.
